_note: Enchs. Not enchantments — `PieceKind::Enchantment` is thirteen catalogue pieces laid under the grid, and this is the other thing, which is the book's own word for it (the ench economy, p. 119). An ench has no shape and goes on no grid: it bolts to a component you already own, and it comes off. Everything one does is a number the engine already had, so nothing here retunes combat.
_price: What a counter charges, and it is two thousand for any of them — the van's three and the sand cart's five alike. An ench is the last thing a character buys rather than the next: the licence is two thousand as well now, and what separates the cart's five from the van's three is not money, it is the flat they are on and the thing standing in front of them.

enchs.name: Plug Energy Tap
enchs.blurb: Four hundred of these were made and three hundred and ninety-one were recalled. The recall notice is on the side of the tap, printed under the tap, where you have to take the tap off to read it.

enchs.name: Grungo Elastic Band
enchs.blurb: Cut off the tree in one piece and sold in eleven. Kaklon's own note says it goes back to the length it was, and does not say when.

enchs.name: The Ponkey Turn
enchs.blurb: Ponkey Dong scored a five, a two and a negative seven, and the negative seven was for the deadlift. Nobody has explained where the turn came from. Kaklon sells it as a bolt-on and does not explain it either.

enchs.name: Sneel Bearing
enchs.blurb: Stainless. Eleven of them in a tin and the tin says twelve, which Kaklon has been asked about four times and has answered once.

enchs.name: The Yodregar Index
enchs.blurb: One card out of a library of every thought anybody has had. The thought on this card is somebody working out, over nine lines, what the thing they are holding is for. It was not filed under gear.

enchs.name: The Chonga Swing
enchs.blurb: Jimmy Chonga hit one thing with it, in the ninth, and the bat did not come back down in one piece. There are four of these and Kaklon's people have written NOT A BAT on all four. It is a bat.

enchs.name: The Wextreen Correction
enchs.blurb: Nine surveys of the reach and no two agree. The tenth does not agree either, but it is the only one that says by how much, and a fitter who reads it can set a bearing off it. It has been right about four acres for eleven years.

enchs.name: The Hooper's Allowance
enchs.blurb: A hoop is cut long and then taken in. The allowance is how much longer, and the woman at Kettleworks has cut eleven thousand of them and never once measured one. She will tell you the number if you turn a kettle for her.

enchs.name: The Sand Glass
enchs.blurb: Iron dust from under the flat, run through a lens and set. It is heavier than the thing it is set into and the fitter who sells it says that is the point, twice, before you have asked.

enchs.name: The Ninth Bearing
enchs.blurb: Cut to a survey nobody has been able to repeat. It sits wrong in the hand and true in the housing, and the ninth surveyor is on record as having thrown one into the water.

enchs.name: The Long Measure
enchs.blurb: A chain of ninety-nine links where the tenth, the fortieth and the ninetieth are a different metal. Whoever made it was counting something, and the cart will not say what.

enchs.name: The Stopped Clock
enchs.blurb: It stopped at eleven and has been sold four times since, each time by somebody explaining that this is not a fault. It is not a fault. It is what you are buying.

enchs.name: The One Swing In The Flat
enchs.blurb: Somebody went out onto the sand with this and came back without it, and then went out again and came back with it. There is one mark on it. There was one thing out there.
